claims.evidence: Release: NIH-funded study, losartan boosts brown fat activity in mice, and increased metabolic activity in brown fat cells. 'Early-stage' is a reasonable characterisation but not a quoted statement.
Release: connection found through analysis of over 100,000 patients.
Increased energy expenditure/oxygen consumption in mice; directly increased metabolic activity of brown fat cells.
Release says losartan boosts brown adipose tissue activity in mice, enhancing metabolism.
'initially discovered the connection ... through an analysis of over 100,000 patients' is in the release.
Release: losartan directly increased metabolic activity in brown fat cells.
Patient analysis plus mouse and cell work; release itself describes mice and brown fat cells.
Retrieved text: lead author suggests brown fat stimulation could be possible even in people with normal blood pressure; 'practical way' / repurposing wording not found.
claims.newSentence: The lead author suggests the drug could allow brown fat to be stimulated even in people with normal blood pressure, though this has been shown only in mice and cells.

notes: Confirmed in NIH release text: '100,000 patients' present; results in mice and brown fat cells; mechanism separate from blood-pressure lowering. 'Brown fat cells' statement present. Release also mentions link to psychiatric health (not in brief). Retrieved human evidence is observational. Date needs manual check on the page.
